newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT BEAT KNICKS DOWN THE STRETCH TO FORCE SEVENTH GAME.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-HEAT BEAT KNICKS DOWN THE STRETCH TO FORCE SEVENTH GAME.

text.p: Tim Hardaway, Dan Majerle and Alonzo Mourning hit big 3-pointers in a fourth-quarter rally as the Miami Heat beat the New York Knicks 95-90 Friday to force a seventh game in their Eastern Conference semifinals.

The Knicks, down three suspended players including their two leading scorers after Wednesday's melee in Miami, led most of the way in an emotional game before a highly charged Madison Square Garden crowd but the Heat, missing suspended forward P.J. Brown, prevailed in the last eight minutes.
"We got hot at the right time," Heat coach Pat Riley said. "We were reeling most of the game, playing behind."
"They deserved it," said New York point guard Chris Childs. "Their players played better than ours down the stretch. That's the bottom line."

The Heat, who had trailed 3-1 in the best-of-seven series, can advance to the conference finals against the Chicago Bulls with a victory in Miami on Sunday, but they will have to do it again without Brown.

The Knicks, looking for another shot at their Chicago rivals, will get back centre Patrick Ewing and guard Allan Houston -- nearly half their playoff offensive production -- as well as backup guard Charlie Ward, but lose forward Larry Johnson and guard John Starks, the NBA Sixth Man of the Year.

Mourning, whose 3-pointer from the top of the circle with 1:16 left in the game was what New York coach Jeff Van Gundy called "the real backbreaker," led all scorers with 28 points, and added nine rebounds and three blocked shots.
"He can't make a free throw, but he drilled that one," Riley said of his center's surprise 3-pointer.
"Whatever the defence presented, we just took advantage iof it," said Mourning, who was just 7-of-14 from the foul line.

Hardaway, who hit two treys in a row to bring the Heat into a 74-74 tie with 5:47 to go, had 20 points, eight assists and six rebounds. Majerle, who also had two threes in a row during the Heat's decisive 18-7 run, scored 18.
"I don't think we come close to winning the game unless we hit those four, five shots," said Riley.
"You have to give Miami credit," said Van Gundy. "They made a lot of big shots down the stretch."

Mourning came up big on defence, too, blocking Buck Williams's pointblank drive to the basket from behind with 3:56 to go as Majerle flashed in front of the Knick forward, who was thrown into a starting role in Ewing's absence.
"Mourning's presence in the paint was a key factor," said Van Gundy. "He made a huge block on Buck going to the basket."
"I don't care who blocked it, it was blocked," said Mourning. "I got a hand on it, I think. Somebody else might have got a hand on it."
Childs led New York with 22 points and nine assists. Johnson had 20 points and nine rebounds, Charles Oakley 18 and 12 and Starks 16 and 11.
Van Gundy refused to dwell on the absence of Ewing, Houston and Ward, even though he said it far outweighed Miami's loss of "role-player" Brown.
"We had more than enough to win with," said Van Gundy. "We had a good effort but we can't be satisfied with a good effort."

None of the Knicks admitted to being tired but Mourning was willing to grant that the nine-man New York team -- eight played -- might have suffered fatigue in the fourth quarter. "There's a possibility they did wear down," he said.
"To tell the truth I think this was the toughest game of the whole series," Mourning added.
With a charged-up crowd roaring, the Knicks went up by 10 points after the first quarter. They led by four points at 44-40 at halftime and two at 66-64 heading into the final quarter.

"It was an emotional game. The crowd was behind us. They did their part, we just didn't do ours, especially me," said Starks, who had a whopping seven turnovers. "I didn't come out and have a good game."
Miami led for the first time at 68-67 on a dunk by Mourning with 9:36 to go, and after New York went back up 72-68, Hardaway started the 18-7 run with a 3-pointer with 7:17 remaining.
"We struggled offensively the last eight to 10 minutes," said Van Gundy.
"We got complacent," said Childs. "They wanted it more.
Majerle was not gloating about the win. "Doesn't say a lot until we win the next game," he said.
"We're going to gear it up, get some players back and go down there and win, and go on to Chicago," said Williams.
"It's one game and somebody's season will be over," said Childs. "It's not going to be ours."
"It comes down to the ultimate game," said Riley.
